subject: Post-call: procurement route, PO vs card & trial billing start
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Judy Summers <judy.summers@bluefield.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: procurement route, PO vs card & trial billing start

Hi Judy / Bluefield team — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

What we covered:
- Primary success criteria for trial: 1) 1M tokens processed over 30 days across two product flows; 2) 95th-percentile latency < 350ms for inference on the LLM endpoints; 3) SSO + audit logs validated for two pilot users.
- Procurement options you asked about: card, PO (standard paper PO), or marketplace (AWS Marketplace).
- Commercial path preference: you indicated procurement typically wants a PO for vendor spend > $25k / year.

Open items / asks (action owners):
1) Bluefield to confirm preferred payment route (card vs PO vs marketplace) and procurement contact — Judy to share by EOD Wed (Aug 5).
2) Redwood to send firm quote + starter SOW for PO routing (Ben) — attached: Redwood-Quote-Bluefield-20260803.pdf, Bluefield-SOW-draft-20260803.docx.
3) Redwood & Bluefield to agree billing start milestone: suggested option A — billing start when trial usage exceeds the baseline threshold (see below); option B — fixed start date after pilot handoff.

Billing threshold options (we recommend Option A for predictable conversion):
- Option A (usage-triggered): Start billing when cumulative trial usage >= 1,000,000 tokens OR when Bluefield signals GA acceptance in writing.
- Option B (fixed start): Start billing on first day of the calendar month following the pilot end (recommended if procurement insists on specific invoice windows).

Next meeting: propose Fri Aug 6 11:00am PT to lock down PO details and billing start. Please confirm.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood-Quote-Bluefield-20260803.pdf (quote), Bluefield-SOW-draft-20260803.docx (SOW draft)

From: Judy Summers <judy.summers@bluefield.io>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@bluefield.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement route, PO vs card & trial billing start

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few quick notes from procurement: 

- Our default is PO for any contract > $10k / quarter. Marketplace is preferred only when vendor provides the exact SKU and pricing we can map; I don't think Redwood's current offer maps cleanly to our AWS procurement flow.
- I'll be the single point of contact for PO paperwork; looped in procurement@bluefield.io for signature.
- For the trial-to-paid trigger, procurement prefers a fixed start date tied to an internal billing cycle. That said, we can discuss a hybrid: a usage-triggered conversion with a cap date (i.e., if threshold not hit by X date, start billing on Y).

Action: I'm confirming internally whether we can do a hybrid. Expect an update by EOD Wed (Aug 5). In the meantime, please send a PO-friendly quote (net-30, include Redwood vendor details + W-9).

-Judy
Judy Summers
Head of Product Operations, Bluefield Analytics
judy.summers@bluefield.io

- Trial conversion: usage-triggered at >= 1,000,000 tokens OR latest by Sep 1, 2026 (whichever comes first).
- Billing cadence: Net 30 after invoice; invoice to be generated when conversion triggers.
- Payment method for first invoice: PO (we will issue a PO number once SOW/quote are finalized).

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Judy — great to confirm the hybrid path. Two small clarifications from Redwood's side: 

1) Token measurement: we'll provide a daily usage export and a short post-trial report summarizing cumulative tokens by flow. That will be the trigger artifact for Option A.
2) Trial cap: to avoid unexpected charges, we'll put a safety cap in the SOW that prevents automatic billing above 1.2M tokens without explicit sign-off.
